title: When the Semester Breaks
premise: Silas Hartwell has spent two years running an anonymous coding account that dismantles the school's beloved traditions from the inside, and he's convinced no one can trace it. But when Ms. Okafor pairs him with Wren Castellanos — his academic rival and the daughter of the family whose foundation funds the school — for a semester project, his anonymity begins to crack. As they build a championship entry together, Silas discovers the account's leaks have been quietly devastating Wren's family, forcing him to choose between the legacy of resentment he inherited from his late mother and the person standing in front of him. In the end, Silas publicly claims the account at the championship finals, loses the competition but wins something harder: forgiveness, a partnership rebuilt on truth, and the memory of his mother finally laid to rest.
about_author: Paloma Vane is the pen name of a former debate-team captain who now writes stories about teenagers who say everything online and nothing out loud. She lives near a college town where semester breaks never come soon enough.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Variable
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. On the first day of senior year, Silas posts another takedown of the school's Hartwell-era traditions under his secret handle, then watches Ms. Okafor announce semester-long paired projects. The emotional beat: smug control curdling into dread when she reads the pairings aloud — his name beside Wren Castellanos's.

chapters.title: Assigned Enemies
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Silas/Wren. Forced to share a lab table, they negotiate a truce: build the autonomous drone for the regional STEM championship, split the credit, speak as little as possible. Wren is sharp, exhausted, and hiding something behind her perfect posture. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition of a fellow performer.

chapters.title: What the Foundation Built
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren works late in her father's foundation office, where budget cuts are quietly gutting the scholarship program Silas's anonymous account keeps defending. She notices her father flinching at his phone every time the handle trends. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture in her loyalty to her family's story.

chapters.title: Debugging at Midnight
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. A code session runs past midnight; Wren falls asleep mid-sentence and Silas sees the exhaustion beneath her armor. He almost tells her about the account. Instead he deletes a draft post targeting the foundation. Emotional beat: guilt arriving like a compile error he can't suppress.

chapters.title: His Mother's Last Repository
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Cleaning out his late mother's files, Silas finds she once worked for the Castellanos foundation — and was pushed out after questioning its spending. His anonymous crusade was inheritance, not choice. Emotional beat: grief reframed as motive, and the terrifying question of whether revenge is what she'd have wanted.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. A private foundation memo appears online, sourced to the anonymous account, and Wren's father spirals toward pulling the school's funding entirely. Wren traces the posting pattern with a coder's eye — and lands on a suspect list of one. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into investigation.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Wren confronts Silas with timestamps and IP logs; he can't lie fast enough. The partnership shatters days before the championship, and she reports him to Ms. Okafor. Emotional beat: the collision both have been building toward, landing harder than either predicted.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (Obviously)
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Silas isolates himself, ready to let the drone die and the account go quiet forever — until he rereads his mother's final email: 'Say it out loud or it doesn't count.' Emotional beat: rock bottom becoming a decision point rather than an ending.

chapters.title: Championship Finals
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. At regionals, Silas takes the stage alone, demos the drone they built together, and publicly claims the anonymous account — apologizing to Wren by name before the whole auditorium. They don't win. Emotional beat: public vulnerability traded for private integrity, the climax paying off every hidden thread.

chapters.title: The Semester That Broke Open
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, closing chapter. Weeks later, Wren brings Silas a revised proposal: the foundation will fund the scholarship program if he helps audit it honestly, together. They restart the project — not for a trophy. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved not by choosing one, but by making them the same thing.
